verbs.text: Stretched for miles in every direction

sentences.text: Towering, glass-fronted skyscrapers soared above the streets, their summits lost in low cloud.
The glittering city skyline blazed against the night sky like a circuit board laid on velvet.
Commuters surged towards the station along teeming, congested pavements, each sealed inside a private hurry.
At six o'clock, office workers streamed out of the underground and scattered into the dusk.
Endless, gridlocked traffic crawled through the city centre, exhausts smoking in the cold.
Horns blared from every direction, sharpening the incessant, deafening roar of the streets.
Somewhere a siren wailed in the distance, and he quickened his pace.
The vast, sprawling metropolis stretched for miles in every direction, a grey tide lapping at the hills.
The windows of the office towers caught the setting sun and turned the whole avenue to gold.
Cyclists wove through the traffic with the careless grace of swallows.
Traders jostled for space in the noisy, bustling market, their cries tangling overhead.
A train rumbled beneath their feet, and the pavement shivered.
Grey, monolithic tower blocks loomed on either side, shutting out all but a strip of sky.
Thick, acrid fumes hung over the rooftops like a soiled blanket.
Tables and chairs spilled onto the pavement outside every café.
Long after midnight, her footsteps echoed between the buildings, the only sound in a city holding its breath.
Garish, flashing neon signs pulsed in the darkness above the theatre doors.
Brilliantly lit shopfronts lined the boulevard, each one a small stage.
The sound of a violin drifted on the evening air from a quiet, leafy square behind the shops.
Even at midnight the city throbbed with life.
A single lamp flickered and buzzed at the mouth of the dark, narrow alley.
Dim, amber street lamps stained the empty, rain-slicked streets a sickly orange.
A wide, tree-lined avenue ran from the station to the park, straight as a ruled line.
The imposing, soot-stained cathedral stood at the city's heart, its spire still taller than the banks.
He turned into the squalid, derelict backstreets, where broken windows stared like empty sockets.
Elegant stone bridges stepped across the river, their lamps doubled in the dark water.
Among so many hurrying strangers, she had never felt so completely alone.
Early on Sunday the city lay calm and washed, and only the pigeons were awake.
Rain lashed the pavements and the wind funnelled between the tower blocks, turning umbrellas inside out.
Litter skittered along the gutters and gathered in doorways like drifts of dirty snow.
